kjv.text: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:

bsb.text: Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.

web.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.

flow.text: Henry shows how this verse promises the Messiah will come from Jesse's line, but only after that royal family has been brought very low.

He comes forth out of the *stem,* or *stump,* of Jesse. When the royal family, that had been as a cedar, was cut down, and only the stump of it left, almost levelled with the ground and lost in the grass of the field (Da 4:15), yet it shall sprout again (Job 14:7); nay, it *shall grow out of his roots,* which are quite buried in the earth, and, like the roots of flowers in the winter, have no stem appearing above ground.
The family that once stood tall, like a great cedar, would be cut down to a stump, yet would sprout again from roots buried deep in the earth.

The house of David was reduced and brought very low at the time of Christ's birth, witness the obscurity and poverty of Joseph and Mary. The Messiah was thus to begin his estate of humiliation, for submitting to which he should be highly exalted, and would thus give early notice that his kingdom was not of this world.

morning.say: Notice how the Messiah comes not in earthly power, but through a humbled, hidden line.
morning.phrase: shall grow out of his roots

leads.kjv: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.
And speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD:
